core_job: For a designer or maker who needs the real colour of a physical thing (fabric, paint, a print, a product), and secondarily for photographers: point the camera at it, or open a photo, and get a trustworthy colour. Keep it in an on-device swatchbook, build palettes from it (k-means in CIELAB, with each colour's share of the picture), and export real .ase/.gpl/CSS/JSON files or a PNG swatch card. Histogram, EXIF and grading sit on one Photo screen; the shot planner stays as 'Light'. Baseline at base_sha: flutter analyze is clean and flutter test passes 1072 tests (run with --no-pub; pubspec.lock was unchanged).
signature: Paper-White Correction. Tap a sheet of white paper (or a grey card) in the frame. Photriya samples the paper and the target from the same camera frame, so automatic white balance cannot drift between the two readings. It corrects the target to neutral light by per-channel division in linear sRGB, normalised so the paper reads as white. It estimates the light (McCamy CCT, plus a Duv check that the paper really looks white), shows 'As seen' and 'Corrected' side by side with the ΔE2000 between them, and warns honestly when the paper is overexposed, too dark or not neutral. The same works on a photo, and there it can become the 'Neutralise' stage of the existing ColorGrade matrix. Everything runs on-device; there is no API and no key. Competitors were checked only through the keyless iTunes Search API (web search is disabled here). Adobe Capture already advertises 'Looks' grading transfer, so that would not be distinct. Pantone Connect advertises camera calibration only with its separate Color Match Card. Whether competitors lack paper-reference correction: competitor not verified.
must: M1 Core capture works on iPhone. By reading the code and the pinned camera_avfoundation 0.9.19 source: the app requests yuv420, iOS delivers 2-plane NV12, and capture_screen.dart:235 returns null when there are fewer than 3 planes. So the live readout likely never shows a colour on iPhone (not verified on a device). Fix it with bgra8888 on iOS or NV12 support. Add pure sampler and preview-to-sensor mapping functions with fixture tests, plus a save-then-confirm capture.

M2 Signature: Paper-White Correction, in a pure reference_correction.dart: sRGB/XYZ/Lab, the correction, McCamy CCT, Krystek Duv, reference quality flags, and CIEDE2000 tested against Sharma 2005 pairs. Camera UI: W reference ring, As seen and Corrected chips, Kelvin estimate, ΔE, plain-language warnings. The same in photo mode. New nullable Hive fields. Delete the made-up '4500 + n*-1200' Kelvin formula; Kelvin is shown only for the light.

M3 Depth: one Swatchbook replaces Library, History, Portfolio and Analytics, with search, filters (Corrected/Camera/Photo/Starred), notes and swipe-to-delete with undo. On-device deterministic k-means palettes from photos, with weights. Real exports: binary .ase (replacing the fake 'ASE data copied' text), .gpl, CSS, JSON and a PNG swatch card through the share sheet, all with byte-level tests.

M4 One Photo bench for a picked photo, with segments Colours (tap to sample, paper white, palette), Grade (ColorGrade plus 'Neutralise from paper white' gains plus a live histogram of the graded result), Histogram and Info (EXIF). It replaces the standalone histogram, EXIF and colour-grading routes; their logic and tests are kept and adapted. The Shot Planner stays as 'Light'.

M5 Remove what isn't this app: DALL-E playground and openai_service, the AI copilot and OpenAI key settings, Academy/Learn/Blogs/Quizzes, the Discover hub, Portfolio, Analytics, Collage, Watermark, Frames, the photo-library browser with its dead thumbnails, all Supabase/Google/Apple sign-in (it syncs nothing and only gates local Analytics), the isPremium PRO badge (no IAP exists) and the unused dependencies. Fix the false purpose strings (NSMotionUsageDescription claims blur reduction, but sensors_plus is unused) and drop the library-read and Android media permissions. Add a 'no residue' grep test and a router route-set test.

M6 Honest states: camera denied or absent, with 'Open a photo instead'; a frame-timeout message; an empty Swatchbook with no seeded samples; a banner when storage is unavailable; and an offline statement (the app needs no network except ads). A widget test for each.

M7 Own identity: a neutral viewing-booth grey theme (light bg #ECECEA, surface #F8F8F7, ink #1B1B1A, accent #C8186E; dark bg #181817, surface #252524, accent #E2509A; collision-checked by grep, contrast computed), following the system setting instead of forced dark. Bundled Archivo variable for UI and Fragment Mono for values (both OFL, fetched with HTTP 200). Paint-chip shape language with radius 2 and hairlines. Home is the Swatchbook with a shutter button, with no NavigationBar or floating tab bar, and Cupertino-adaptive controls on iOS. The ad banner only at the foot of the Swatchbook. Reachable first-launch onboarding about paper white (no 'Get started'). Own settings copy, keeping Privacy choices. A new icon and a #ECECEA splash.

M8 Proven: flutter analyze clean and all tests pass, including the new ones; tests are deleted only together with deleted code. The screenshot integration test no longer signs in with the QA account. Commit path-limited without touching fastlane/** or project.pbxproj (others' edits) and push to main. Simulator launch screenshots plus a release-build launch. A physical-iPhone run only if a device is attached, otherwise reported 'not verified'. The 2.1(a) crash root cause is not verified because the Apple crash log is not on this machine.
